issues.legal_issue: Joint-family property retains its joint-family character after severance of family status until it is partitioned.
material_facts: The property at issue had been treated as joint-family property.
A family member notified the others of an intention to sever the joint-family status, but the property had not yet been partitioned.
issues.conclusion: Severance of joint-family status alone did not convert the property into the personal property of any member; it retained its joint-family character until partition.
issues.legal_principle: The character of joint-family property does not change merely upon severance of family status. A member cannot unilaterally convert joint-family property into personal property; the property retains its character while it remains unpartitioned.

predicates.joint_family_property_exists: The property was held or treated as an asset of the joint family.
predicates.family_status_severed: A member caused or notified a severance of the joint-family status.
predicates.property_not_partitioned: The property remained undivided among the family members.

issues.definition: When joint-family property remains undivided after family status is severed, it continues to have joint-family character.

issues.legal_issue: Income received under a managing-agency arrangement formed for the benefit of a joint family belongs to the family while the arrangement continues.
material_facts: Two family members joined a partnership on behalf of and for the benefit of the joint family.
The partnership obtained the company's managing agency, and the family members received commissions and other remuneration under that arrangement.
The receipts were treated as joint-family income, entered in the family accounts, and reported as such before a family dispute arose.
One family member later claimed the income personally and sought to retain part of it for services rendered.
issues.conclusion: Commissions, directors' fees, and managing-agent remuneration received under the arrangement while it continued belonged to the joint family; the member could not retain part as personal income merely because he performed services or declared his intention to treat the income as personal.
issues.legal_principle: The partnership and managing-agency interests were held on behalf of the family, so income earned under those arrangements remained family property while the arrangements continued. Joint-family property cannot be converted into personal property by unilateral declaration. The distinction between a return on family investment and compensation for an individual's services, explained in Raj Kumar Singh Hukum Chandji v. Commissioner of Income Tax, Madhya Pradesh, [1971] 1 SCR 748, informs the characterization of remuneration; the Court also considered the managing-agency agreement's termination under section 87A(2) of the Companies Act.

rule.if: joint_family_partition_proceeding and family_members_joined_partnership_for_family_benefit and partnership_held_managing_agency and income_received_under_continuing_agency and income_treated_as_family_income

predicates.joint_family_partition_proceeding: The dispute concerns the division or accounting of property claimed to belong to a joint family.
predicates.family_members_joined_partnership_for_fa: Family members joined the partnership as representatives of the family and for its benefit.
predicates.partnership_held_managing_agency: The partnership, rather than an individual family member, held the company's managing-agency arrangement.
predicates.income_received_under_continuing_agency: The disputed income was received under that arrangement while it remained in force.
predicates.income_treated_as_family_income: The family treated the receipts as family income, including in its accounts or tax reporting.

issues.definition: In a joint-family property dispute, income received under a continuing managing-agency arrangement held by a partnership formed for the family's benefit is family property when the family treated it as such.

issues.legal_issue: Remuneration for an individual managing director's services is personal income when the appointment follows family disruption and the former family-linked managing agency has ended.
material_facts: The managing-agency agreement ended and was not renewed.
The joint family had completely disrupted before the individual was appointed managing director.
The company amended its articles and appointed the individual to provide services; the former managing-agency firm and its partners did not effectively challenge those steps.
The Court found that the appointment was not a return on the family's investment and that the remuneration compensated the individual's services.
issues.conclusion: The managing director's remuneration was his personal income and was not accountable to the joint family.
issues.legal_principle: Under Raj Kumar Singh Hukum Chandji v. Commissioner of Income Tax, Madhya Pradesh, [1971] 1 SCR 748, remuneration is family income when in substance it is a return for family investment, but personal income when it is compensation for the coparcener's services. The Court applied that distinction and considered that the managing-agency agreement had ended under section 87A(2) of the Companies Act before the appointment.

rule.if: joint_family_partition_proceeding and managing_agency_ended and family_disrupted_before_appointment and individual_appointed_for_services and remuneration_compensates_individual_services and appointment_not_return_on_family_investment

predicates.joint_family_partition_proceeding: The dispute concerns whether income belongs to a joint family whose property is being divided or accounted for.
predicates.managing_agency_ended: The family-linked managing-agency arrangement had ceased before the individual received the disputed remuneration.
predicates.family_disrupted_before_appointment: The joint family had completely ceased to exist before the individual was appointed to the later role.
predicates.individual_appointed_for_services: The company appointed the individual to perform services in his personal capacity.
predicates.remuneration_compensates_individual_serv: The remuneration was paid for services rendered or to be rendered by the individual.
predicates.appointment_not_return_on_family_investm: The appointment and remuneration were not shown to be a return for the family's investment in the business.

issues.definition: When a family-linked agency has ended and an individual is appointed after family disruption to provide services for remuneration that is not a return on family investment, that remuneration is personal income.

issues.legal_issue: Shares purchased with joint-family funds while the family is joint belong to the joint family.
material_facts: The family purchased shares in the company while it remained joint.
The purchase price for the shares was paid from joint-family funds.
The parties accepted that the initially acquired shares were joint-family property, and the Court also found that later shares paid for from family funds belonged to the family.
issues.conclusion: The shares acquired with joint-family funds belonged to the joint family and were to be shared equally among its three branches.
issues.legal_principle: Property acquired with joint-family funds while the family is joint forms part of the joint-family property. The Court applied this principle to the shares for which payment from family funds was established.

predicates.joint_family_partition_proceeding: The dispute concerns the division of property claimed to belong to a joint family.
predicates.shares_acquired_for_joint_family: The shares were acquired while the family was joint and for its benefit.
predicates.joint_family_funds_paid_purchase_price: The purchase price for the shares came from joint-family funds.

issues.definition: Shares acquired for a joint family with its funds are treated as joint-family property in a partition dispute.

issues.legal_issue: Shares acquired individually after disruption of the joint family do not belong to the family absent proof that family funds paid for them.
material_facts: Other shares were acquired after the joint family had completely disrupted.
The evidence did not establish that joint-family funds paid for those later acquisitions.
The shares were acquired by individual family members or their children.
issues.conclusion: The later shares for which no payment from joint-family funds was established were not joint-family property.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished shares acquired with joint-family funds from later acquisitions made after the family had disrupted. It found no proof that the joint family funded the latter acquisitions and no basis to treat them as family property.

predicates.joint_family_partition_proceeding: The dispute concerns whether assets belong to a joint family whose property is being divided.
predicates.shares_acquired_after_family_disruption: The shares were acquired after the joint family had completely disrupted.
predicates.no_proof_of_joint_family_funding: The evidence did not establish that joint-family funds paid for the shares.

issues.definition: Shares acquired after a family has disrupted are not treated as family property when there is no proof that family funds paid for them.

issues.legal_issue: Personal possession of ornaments, jewellery, and utensils does not establish that they remain joint-family property when the evidence shows no family ownership and indicates prior partition.
material_facts: The record did not establish that ornaments, jewellery, or utensils in any party's possession belonged to the joint family.
The available materials suggested that these movable items had already been partitioned.
issues.conclusion: The items in each party's possession were to be treated as that party's own property, with no further joint-family claim between the parties.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to treat movable property as joint-family property without evidence establishing family ownership, particularly where the evidence indicated that the items had already been partitioned.

predicates.joint_family_partition_proceeding: The dispute concerns claims to property in a joint-family partition.
predicates.no_evidence_of_joint_family_ownership: The record does not establish that the disputed movable items belonged to the joint family.
predicates.evidence_indicates_prior_partition: The available evidence indicates that the items had already been divided among the family members.

issues.definition: In a joint-family partition dispute, movable items in a party's possession are treated as that party's property when family ownership is unproved and prior partition is indicated.

issues.legal_issue: A court may fix a reasonable sum for acknowledged joint-family cash when the amount cannot reliably be determined and further accounting would prolong the dispute.
material_facts: The evidence established that some joint-family cash was kept in a room.
A receiver counted an amount substantially below the amount claimed by one party, and the record lacked dependable material to determine the exact total.
The litigation had continued for decades, and the parties asked the Court to fix an amount rather than order further accounts.
issues.conclusion: The Court fixed a final sum in the decree, taking account of the claimant's share of the cash, instead of directing further accounting; the claimant had no further claim on that account.
issues.legal_principle: To avoid prolonging long-running litigation where the existence of joint-family cash was established but its amount could not be reliably determined, the Court used the record and the parties' submissions to fix a reasonable amount in the final decree.

rule.if: joint_family_partition_proceeding and some_joint_family_cash_established and exact_amount_unreliable and further_accounting_would_prolong_litigation

predicates.joint_family_partition_proceeding: The dispute concerns division of joint-family property.
predicates.some_joint_family_cash_established: The evidence establishes that some cash belonged to the joint family.
predicates.exact_amount_unreliable: The evidence does not provide a dependable basis to determine the exact amount of that cash.
predicates.further_accounting_would_prolong_litigat: Further accounting would materially prolong already lengthy litigation.

issues.definition: When a partition court can establish that joint-family cash existed but cannot reliably determine its amount, it may fix a reasonable sum rather than order further accounting that would prolong the dispute.
